question.text: Consider the function $\mathrm{f}$ in $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R}-\left\{\frac{2}{3}\right\}$ defined as $f(x)=\frac{4 x+3}{6 x-4}$, then $f^{-1}$ is equal to

solution.text:
Given $f(x)=\frac{4 x+3}{6 x-4}$
Let $y=\frac{4 x+3}{6 x-4}$,
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 6 x y-4 y=4 x+3 \Rightarrow x(6 y-4)=3+4 y \\
& \Rightarrow x=\frac{3+4 y}{6 y-4} \\
& f^{-1}(x)=\frac{3+4 x}{6 x-4}
\end{aligned}$
